turns.content:
Build a multi-page website for "Artisan Goods Co.",
a handmade crafts shop. I need:
- Homepage with a hero banner, featured products
  section, and a newsletter signup
- Product catalog page with category filters
  (pottery, textiles, woodwork, jewelry) and a grid
  of product cards with images, names, and prices
- About page with our story, team member profiles
  with photos, and a mission statement
- Shared navigation header and footer across all
  pages
Use React Router for page navigation. Products
should be fetched from an API endpoint.

I'll build the full Artisan Goods Co. website systematically. Let me start with Phase 1 — all setup tasks in parallel.Now let me run all Phase 1 tasks in parallel — logo generation, media searches, fonts, and colors:Phase 1 complete. Now Phase 2 — API, Header, Footer in parallel:Now let me build all Phase 2 items in parallel — products API, Header, and Footer:Now register the products API in entry.ts and update RootLayout:Now verify the API works, then build all three pages in parallel:API is live. Now mark it done and build all three pages in parallel:Now building all three pages simultaneously:Now update routes.tsx with all three routes and loaders:Now update the SEO routes and check the lib/seo-routes.ts:Now mark all remaining todos done and offer the logo actions:The full Artisan Goods Co. website is built. Here's what's live:

**Homepage** — Full-bleed hero with warm overlay, animated headline and CTAs, 4 featured products pulled from the API, a stats band, and an asymmetric terracotta newsletter section.

**Product Catalog (`/products`)** — Sticky category filter tabs (All / Pottery / Textiles / Woodwork / Jewelry), a responsive 3-column grid with hover lift + image scale, color-coded category badges, and an empty state for filtered results.

**About Page (`/about`)** — Full-bleed hero, 2-column story layout with pull quote, a dark mission statement band, and a team grid with photos for Elena, Marcus, and Priya.

**Shared Header & Footer** — Sticky header with logo, nav links with animated underlines, mobile hamburger menu, and a rich 4-column footer in deep walnut brown.

input.prompt:
Build a full multi-page website for "Artisan Goods Co.", a handmade crafts shop. Here is the complete design direction and build plan.

PROJECT DETAILS:
- Business: Artisan Goods Co. — handmade crafts shop
- Categories: Pottery, Textiles, Woodwork, Jewelry
- Audience: Craft lovers, gift shoppers, design-conscious consumers
- Goal: Showcase products, tell the brand story, grow newsletter list

DESIGN DIRECTION:
Warm, artisanal aesthetic that feels handcrafted and authentic — like browsing a well-curated maker's market. Rich earthy tones, generous whitespace, and editorial typography create a premium yet approachable feel. Nothing corporate or generic.

LAYOUT TYPE: Standard
Full header navigation and footer across all pages.

VISUAL DIRECTION:
- Color: Warm earth tones — terracotta, warm cream/off-white, deep walnut brown, sage green accent. NOT cool grays or generic white. Warm off-white (#FAF7F2 range) as base background.
- Typography: Pair a refined serif (Playfair Display or Cormorant Garamond) for headings with a clean humanist sans (DM Sans or Nunito) for body. Generous line-height, elegant hierarchy.
- Layout: Editorial and asymmetric where possible. Full-bleed hero. Product grid with subtle hover lifts. NO icon grids for features.

VISUAL ELEMENTS:
- Primary: Photography (product shots, lifestyle, artisan hands at work)
- Style: Warm-toned, natural light, textured backgrounds
- Application: Hero full-bleed, product cards, team profile photos
- Logo: Generate a logo using the media-logo skill — wordmark style with a small handcrafted icon (e.g. a simple leaf, clay vessel, or woven texture mark). Warm brown on cream.

MOTION DESIGN:
- Level: Subtle
- Effects: Fade-in on scroll for sections (350ms ease-out), hover lift on product cards (translateY -4px + shadow), smooth underline on nav links, gentle image scale on card hover (1.03)
- Personality: Warm and unhurried — nothing snappy or corporate

SECTION-SPECIFIC:

Hero (Homepage):
- Full-bleed image with warm overlay, large serif headline, short tagline, two CTAs ("Shop Now" → /products, "Our Story" → /about)
- Subtle fade-in entrance animation

Featured Products (Homepage):
- Section title "Handpicked for You" in serif
- Grid of 4 featured products (pulled from API, flagged as featured)
- Cards: product image, name, category badge, price, hover lift effect
- "View All Products" link below grid

Newsletter Signup (Homepage):
- Warm terracotta band, NOT a centered-on-band generic CTA
- Asymmetric layout: large serif headline left, email input + button right
- Subtle entrance animation

Header:
- Logo left, nav links center (Home, Shop, About), optional CTA button right ("Shop Now")
- Sticky on scroll with subtle shadow
- Mobile hamburger menu
- Warm cream background, walnut brown text

Footer:
- Multi-column: brand blurb + social links | shop links | about links | newsletter mini-form
- Warm brown background, cream text
- Matches overall artisan quality — not an afterthought

PRODUCT CATALOG PAGE (/products):
- Page title "Our Collection" with serif heading
- Category filter tabs: All | Pottery | Textiles | Woodwork | Jewelry
- Filtering is client-side (filter the loaded data)
- Responsive product grid (3 cols desktop, 2 tablet, 1 mobile)
- Product card: image (aspect-ratio square), product name, category badge (color-coded per category), price
- Hover: lift effect + subtle image scale
- Empty state if no products in category
- Data fetched via route loader from /api/products

ABOUT PAGE (/about):
- Hero: warm full-bleed image, "Our Story" heading
- Story section: 2-column layout — large pull quote left, narrative paragraphs right
- Mission statement: full-width, large serif quote styled prominently, terracotta accent
- Team section: "Meet the Makers" heading, grid of team member cards (photo, name, role, short bio)
- Team photos fetched/searched from media

PRODUCTS API ENDPOINT:
Create `src/server/api/products.ts` and register in `src/server/entry.ts`.

Return an array of ~12 products across all 4 categories. Each product:
```ts
{
  id: string,
  name: string,
  category: 'pottery' | 'textiles' | 'woodwork' | 'jewelry',
  price: number,
  image: string, // use a placeholder image URL from picsum.photos with a seed
  description: string,
  featured: boolean
}
```

Use picsum.photos for images: `https://picsum.photos/seed/{productId}/600/600`

Example products:
- Pottery: "Speckled Ceramic Mug" $28, "Terracotta Planter" $45, "Stoneware Bowl Set" $65
- Textiles: "Hand-woven Throw Blanket" $89, "Linen Table Runner" $38, "Macramé Wall Hanging" $72
- Woodwork: "Walnut Serving Board" $55, "Oak Candle Holder" $32, "Carved Wooden Spoon Set" $24
- Jewelry: "Hammered Silver Ring" $48, "Ceramic Bead Necklace" $62, "Copper Leaf Earrings" $35

Mark 4 as featured: the mug, throw blanket, serving board, silver ring.

ROUTES (src/routes.tsx):
```tsx
[
  { path: '/', element: <HomePage />, loader: homepageLoader },
  { path: '/products', element: <ProductsPage />, loader: productsLoader },
  { path: '/about', element: <AboutPage /> }
]
```

Loaders fetch from /api/products (homepage loader filters featured:true).

BUILD ORDER:

Phase 1 — Setup (run in parallel):
- Generate logo using media-logo skill
- Search for hero images: artisan workshop, handmade ceramics lifestyle, warm natural light crafts
- Search for team member photos: 3 diverse artisan/maker portraits
- Set font stack using fontTheme tool: Playfair Display (headings) + DM Sans (body)
- Set color scheme using colorScheme tool: warm cream base, terracotta primary, walnut brown secondary, sage accent

Phase 2 — API & Structure (run in parallel, after Phase 1):
- Create products API: src/server/api/products.ts + register in entry.ts
- Build Header (sticky, logo, nav, mobile menu)
- Build Footer (multi-column, warm brown bg)
- Update RootLayout to use new Header/Footer

Phase 3 — Pages (after Phase 2):
- Build Homepage (index.tsx): hero, featured products, newsletter
- Build Products page (src/pages/products.tsx): filters + grid
- Build About page (src/pages/about.tsx): story, mission, team

Phase 4 — Routes & Finalize:
- Update src/routes.tsx with all 3 routes + loaders
- Mark all todo items as COMPLETE using todoList tool
- Ask for design feedback using askQuestion

CRITICAL: Build pages LAST — after API, header, footer, fonts, and colors are all in place.

TODO LIST MANAGEMENT:
After completing each major piece, mark the corresponding todo item complete:
- After header/footer: mark "Shared header & footer" complete
- After API: mark "Products API endpoint" complete
- After homepage: mark "Homepage" complete
- After products page: mark "Product catalog page" complete
- After about page: mark "About page" complete

DESIGN FEEDBACK:
After showing the site, use askQuestion to ask:
- Question: "How does the site look?"
- Suggestions: ["Looks great — ship it!", "Adjust the color palette", "Change the typography", "Add a product detail page", "Add a shopping cart"]

{/* Narrative */}

Artisan Goods Co. was born from a simple frustration: the world was full of beautiful handmade things, but they were scattered across farmers' markets, studio sales, and Instagram feeds — impossible to find in one place.

We started in 2019 with a folding table at a local craft fair and a handful of makers we believed in. Today, we work with over 40 independent artisans across the country, each one vetted not just for the quality of their craft, but for the care they bring to every piece.

Every item in our shop is made by hand. That means slight variations in glaze, grain, and texture — and that's exactly the point. These are not factory goods. They are objects made by people, for people, meant to be used and loved for years.

We ship from our studio in Portland, Oregon, where our small team packs every order by hand, often with a handwritten note from the maker tucked inside.

turns.content: The product catalog page looks good, but I want to make sure the product data isn't just hardcoded directly in the component. Can you confirm that the products page is actually pulling data from the API endpoint or a service module, rather than having all the product names, prices, and details written out inline in the component code?

Let me check both files quickly.Confirmed — the products page has zero hardcoded product data. Here's exactly how it flows:

1. **`src/server/api/products/GET.ts`** — This is the single source of truth. All 12 products (names, prices, descriptions, categories) live here as a data array, served via `GET /api/products`.

2. **`src/routes.tsx`** — The `/products` route has a `loader` that calls `fetchProducts()`, which hits `/api/products` over HTTP before the page renders. The data is injected via React Router's data router pattern.

3. **`src/pages/products.tsx`** — The component contains zero product data. It only calls `useLoaderData()` to receive what the loader fetched, then renders it. The only things defined in the component are UI-level constants (filter labels and category color classes).

The architecture is clean: if you want to change a product name, price, or description, you edit the API handler — the component automatically reflects the change.
